pr_title: Fix some handle leaks in rainforest_raven
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
There were file handle leaks when:
* The component was shutdown or reloaded
* There was a timeout during the initial device opening

Additionally, the device was not closed/reopened when there was a timeout reading regular data.

A test was added to exercise the timeout code. Note that this test actually does wait for the timeout to trigger normally, and therefore takes 5 seconds to complete. If this is not acceptable, I can update the test to explicitly raise a `TimeoutError` immediately.

issue_context.title: ValueError: filedescriptor out of range in select()
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Every time I update Home Assistant and restart the service, my emu2 falls offline with unknown values.

When I ask the integration to reload, I receive

```
2024-02-29 11:59:55.872 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant] Error doing job: Exception in callback SerialTransport._read_ready()
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/asyncio/events.py", line 84, in _run
    self._context.run(self._callback, *self._args)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/serial_asyncio/__init__.py", line 115, in _read_ready
    data = self._serial.read(self._max_read_size)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/serial/serialposix.py", line 565, in read
    ready, _, _ = select.select([self.fd, self.pipe_abort_read_r], [], [], timeout.time_left())
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ValueError: filedescriptor out of range in select()
```

Hmm, maybe there is a handle leak somewhere. Do you run a particularly busy Home Assistant instance? Are there multiple USB or serial devices connected?

I wouldn't say it's particularly busy, but I do have multiple usb devices. I have a Zigbee, Z-Wave, Thread and Emu2 hooked up on the usb bus. 

That said, the Emu2's udev symlink has been stable. I've validated that it has always pointed to the same /dev/ttyACM0 device node.

I've had this happen to me too, where I have had to restart a couple times before my EMU-2 reconnects, though I don't remember exactly what triggered it. I think it was right after updating to 2024.3.0.

Even after getting it to connect, I receive frequent "Unavailable" states throughout the day, making the History graph look very "dotted" with lots of blank gaps in between valid readings.
I didn't get the frequent "Unavailable" states before the 2024.3.0 update.

Here is the error message I receive:

```
DELETED (accidentally copy pasted the error message from the original poster, instead of the one from my installation)
```

My USB devices are:

review_comments: Move time forward instead to trigger a refresh. See other integrations that use a coordinator with tests for examples.
Besides this, I'd make the timeout time a constant so we can easily patch it to 0. We don't want slow tests.
We should assert that the mock device is closed. We can also assert that a coordinator entity have its state set to unavailable.

Set up the integration instead. We shouldn't interact with the coordinator directly as that's an integration detail.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_testing#writing-tests-for-integrations
